description: Hind paw reads as a flat slipper, not the clay's long four-toed paw: toes separate only at the tips (clay: deep clefts over about the front 40 percent of the paw, each toe a long digit with two knuckle bumps), claws barely visible (about 10 mm; clay claws are large dark hooks about a quarter of toe length, curving down past the toe tip to the ground), and a bulbous heel blob where the metatarsus meets the paw (clay: the metatarsus runs straight down into a clean narrow heel).
